Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate includes a short video that appears to demonstrate the Visual Intelligence feature of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Please watch the video below.

macOS 26.7 includes a demo video of the camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered that today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate contains a short video in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to remember the book he is looking at, with Siri's voiceover saying:

The camera itself is not visible in the video, and the earbuds look very similar to the existing AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is the stem, which appears slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also posted the same video on X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch the camera-equipped AirPods, codenamed B790, as early as this year. MacRumors also found references to B790 in this morning's macOS 26.7 release candidate, including code for an "image stream".

It's worth noting that these AirPods are reportedly a separate model from another one that, according to Bloomberg, Apple has been developing under the codename B798, which is expected to launch in 2027.

Given Apple's decision to include this demo video in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to make their official debut at next month's iPhone event.

What do you think of the video? Let us know in the comments.
